title: Autoformalization with Large Language Models
abstract: This paper explores the use of large language models for autoformalization, the process of automatically translating from natural language mathematics to formal specifications and proofs. The authors demonstrate that large language models can correctly translate a significant portion of mathematical competition problems into formal specifications in Isabelle/HOL, and that this process can be used to improve neural theorem provers.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content: Imagine you're trying to translate a math problem from natural language to a formal proof. It's like translating from one language to another, but with precise rules and symbols. Autoformalization is the process of doing this automatically, using large language models. We'll explore how this works and why it matters.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: Large language models, like Codex and PaLM, are trained on vast amounts of text data. We use these models to translate natural language math problems into formal specifications in Isabelle/HOL. The models learn to recognize patterns and generate formal code, even with limited training data.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: We evaluated our approach on the miniF2F benchmark, which consists of 140 algebra problems and 120 number theory problems. Our model achieved a 35.2% proof rate, outperforming the previous state-of-the-art of 29.6%.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: Autoformalization has the potential to revolutionize the field of formal verification and artificial intelligence. By automating the process of translating natural language math problems into formal proofs, we can make mathematics more accessible and efficient.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: Our approach uses in-context learning to fine-tune large language models on a few examples of formalized math problems. This allows the models to learn the patterns and structures of formal mathematics, even with limited training data.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content: We provide a pre-trained model and a dataset of formalized math problems for you to try out our approach. Experiment with different models and datasets to see the potential of autoformalization.
